hub_subtitle: Business English para seguros, reuniões e entrevistas — e o desbloqueio da fala, do primeiro dia ao último

lesson.menu_title: Review and Consolidation -- Twenty Lessons, One Story
lesson.menu_desc: A aula que fecha o bloco — e a única sem nenhuma forma nova. As seis que a Paula já tem voltam juntas, no mesmo lugar, para uma coisa só: escolher a certa sem parar para pensar. Presente para o que é verdade sempre (the client moves goods every day), was/were para como as coisas eram, past simple para o que aconteceu e acabou, was/were + -ing para o que estava acontecendo, going to e will para o que vem depois, e o comparativo para escolher entre duas. A chave não é decorar seis regras: é fazer uma pergunta — que pergunta esta frase responde? —, porque a pergunta escolhe a forma. Seis palavras de revisão (client, report, deadline, goal, claim, quote), a ficha completa do cliente de Santos na tela, o Greg ensaiando a call de Miami, e o produto do dia: a conta inteira contada em cinco frases, sozinha, sem cartão. -- 38 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 20 -- Review and Consolidation
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Paula Morales | Lesson 20 -- Review and Consolidation (Twenty Lessons, One Story)
lesson.grammar_point: review and consolidation -- no new structure: choosing between present simple, past simple, was/were, past continuous, going to and will, and comparatives, by the question the sentence answers

listenings.text: Hi, Paula. David here. Twenty-two years ago I presented a big account alone in Miami for the first time. I was thirty-one, and I was terrified, so I did the worst thing possible: I wrote three pages and I learned them by heart. Word by word. In the room, I said two sentences, and then my head was completely empty. Nothing. I stood there in silence for eleven seconds. Eleven seconds is a very long time when eight people are looking at you. After the meeting, an old broker took me for a coffee, and he was kind but he was honest. He said: nobody in that room wanted a speech. They wanted five things. Who the client is. What the history is. What the loss was. What the numbers say. And what happens next. He wrote them on a paper napkin, five short lines, and he gave it to me. I still do that today, before every presentation. One small card, five sentences, one for each part of the story. And here is why it works, Paula, and this is the only thing I want you to remember: you cannot forget five sentences. And if you lose one of them, the other four are still there, and nobody in the room knows anything was missing. See you soon.

Good morning, Paula. Sofia here. I want to tell you one thing before your lesson today, and then I will leave you alone. In January, in my office, you said one sentence to me. You said: I understand a little, but I cannot speak. I remember it exactly, because I wrote it down. Now listen to this week. On Monday you answered Greg's call in English, at seven in the morning, alone. On Tuesday you read the incident report from the site manager, and you did not ask me for a translation. On Wednesday you compared two quotes and you recommended one, with a reason. On Thursday you called the client and you asked him three questions on the phone. And your report notes are in English now. I have five of them here on my desk. That is one week, Paula. One week. And you did not notice any of it, because it happened slowly, one lesson at a time. Now the practical part. The flight and the hotel for November twelve are booked. You have five minutes with the team, and the reinsurer is in the room. And I want you to hear one thing about that room: it is not a test. Nobody there is waiting for a mistake. They only want to understand the account, and you are the person in this company who knows it best. See you Thursday.

reading.rtitle: Account File — Litoral Cargo Ltda, Santos — prepared for Miami
paras: Litoral Cargo is a logistics company in Santos. It has four warehouses and eighty trucks. The company moves food and machines to the port every day, and it works with three big clients in Europe. Our goal for this account is one single contract for the four warehouses.

In 2019 the company was small. It had two warehouses and thirty trucks, and the first quote was cheap and simple: fire only. In 2022 the company opened warehouse 4 and bought fifty new trucks. The contract was old and the coverage was small, but nobody changed it.

In April a fire started in warehouse 4, at 6:55 in the morning. At that moment the team was loading a truck at door 2, and nobody was using the old machine. Everybody left the building in four minutes and nobody was hurt. We opened the claim the same morning.

Today there are two quotes on the table. Option B is cheaper, but the coverage in Option A is more complete: fire, flood and transport. For this client, Option A is the best choice. The client is going to decide on Thursday, and I will send the final report to Miami before the deadline on Friday.
reading.source: Paula Morales — account file, Litoral Cargo Ltda, Santos — prepared for the Miami team

reading.prompt: What is the main idea of the account file?
choices: It is a price list of the fifty trucks that the company bought in 2022.
It is the whole story of one client on one page: who they are today, how the company was in 2019, the fire in April and what was happening at that moment, and the two quotes for the renewal.
It is an invitation from the Miami team to visit the port of Santos in November.

items: The company had four warehouses in 2019.
f
No. In 2019 it had two warehouses and thirty trucks. It has four warehouses TODAY — and that is the whole difference between had and has.
The team was loading a truck when the fire started.
t
Yes: at 6:55 the team was loading a truck at door 2. That is what was happening around the fire — and it is the line the reinsurer reads first.
Somebody was hurt in the fire.
f
No. Everybody left the building in four minutes and nobody was hurt. That is the first line Miami looks for in any claim.
Option B is more expensive than Option A.
f
No, the other way round. Option B is cheaper — but the coverage in Option A is more complete: fire, flood and transport.
The client is going to decide on Thursday.
t
Yes. The meeting is already in the diary, and that is exactly why the file says is going to decide and not will decide.

bank.label: The five parts of the story / As cinco partes da historia
items: Litoral Cargo is a logistics company in Santos.
In 2019 the company was small.
In April a fire started in warehouse 4.
The team was loading a truck at that moment.
The client is going to decide on Thursday.

bank.label: Closing and next steps / Fechar e o proximo passo
items: Option B is cheaper, but I recommend Option A.
For this client, Option A is the best choice.
I will send the report before the deadline.
My goal is one contract for the four warehouses.
Could you repeat that, please?

items.situation: Greg asks: "Who is this client today?" Answer with a full sentence, in the present.
tips: Litoral Cargo is a logistics company in Santos.
The client has four warehouses and eighty trucks.

items.situation: He asks how the company was in 2019. Answer with two facts.
tips: It had two warehouses and thirty trucks, and the contract was cheap and simple.

items.situation: Say what happened in April, in one sentence, with the time.
tips: In April a fire started in warehouse 4.
A fire started at 6:55 in the morning and it damaged half of the warehouse.

items.situation: The reinsurer asks what the team was doing at that exact moment. Answer.
tips: The team was loading a truck at door 2.
They were working normally, and nobody was using the old machine.

items.situation: The client meeting is already in the diary, and the report is your promise. Say both in one sentence.
tips: The client is going to decide on Thursday, and I will send the report on Friday.
He is going to decide this week, and I will send the final report before the deadline.

items.situation: Greg asks: "So what do you recommend?" Answer in one sentence, with a reason.
tips: Option B is cheaper, but I recommend Option A, because the coverage is more complete.
For this client, Option A is the best choice.
